difference_from_existing.difference: Not QQQ/TQQQ 30-minute momentum on IEX bars: SIP consolidated minute bars, ETF symbol axis of 17, half-hourly noise-band rule from the paper, depth curves.
Old test checked every minute with a persistent band and one symbol; this one uses the paper's HH:00/HH:30 checks, 4x3x3x3x2 versions and 17 symbols.

mechanism_description: Rule-based intraday strategies re-run to minimum effective depth: noise-band momentum (A), first-half-hour to last-half-hour momentum (B), stocks-in-play opening range (C), owner Reversal Trend on 1-minute and 1-hour bars (D).
objective: T-20261006-15: do published intraday rules (noise band, market intraday momentum, stocks-in-play ORB, Reversal Trend) keep a net-of-cost edge in 2024-01-08..2026-10-06 once run at depth (reproduction, faithful rule, three or more scale points, full registered grids, power)?

sources.applicability: Group A rule, parameters (VM 0.5-2, lookback 7/14/28, stop variants, vol target) and the paper cell.
sources.claim: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon (SFI WP 24-97, 2024): SPY intraday momentum with a time-of-day Noise Area = max/min(open, previous close) x (1 +/- VM x sigma), sigma the mean absolute move from the open over the previous 14 days at the same minute; positions are set only at HH:00 and HH:30, stopped by the current band and the VWAP, flat at the close; with volatility targeting (2%, leverage cap 4) 2007-2024 gave 19.6 percent a year, Sharpe 1.33, 1.8 trades a day; the base opposite-band version gave Sharpe 0.61.
sources.core_claim: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon (SFI WP 24-97, 2024): SPY intraday momentum with a time-of-day Noise Area = max/min(open, previous close) x (1 +/- VM x sigma), sigma the mean absolute move from the open over the previous 14 days at the same minute; positions are set only at HH:00 and HH:30, stopped by the current band and the VWAP, flat at the close; with volatility targeting (2%, leverage cap 4) 2007-2024 gave 19.6 percent a year, Sharpe 1.33, 1.8 trades a day; the base opposite-band version gave Sharpe 0.61.
sources.independent_replication: Local H-20260922-07 reproduced 2.2 percent a year and Sharpe 0.30 (persist entries each minute); a third-party automated replication reported 0.41. Not reproduced yet with the half-hourly rule; this iteration does it.
sources.limitations: Author-reported, no out-of-sample split; costs only $0.0045 per share; paper itself says the optimum is VM 1.5 and lookback 90, so 14/1 is not an ex-post optimum.
sources.market_and_period: SPY, 2007-05 to 2024-04, 1-minute IQFeed bars, commission $0.0035 + slippage $0.001 per share
sources.project_applicability: Group A rule, parameters (VM 0.5-2, lookback 7/14/28, stop variants, vol target) and the paper cell.
sources.reflection: Fixes check interval, anchor and stop semantics; the local old test checked every minute, which is not the paper rule.

sources.applicability: Group B predictors (first half-hour with and without overnight, plus the twelfth half-hour) and trading window 15:30-16:00.
sources.claim: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (JFE 2018): the first half-hour return of SPY measured from the previous close predicts the last half-hour return (R2 1.6 percent, 2.6 percent with the twelfth half-hour; out-of-sample 1.2 and 1.8 percent), a sign-timing strategy earns 6.67 percent a year at 6.19 percent volatility, Sharpe 1.08, before costs, 1993-2013.
sources.core_claim: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (JFE 2018): the first half-hour return of SPY measured from the previous close predicts the last half-hour return (R2 1.6 percent, 2.6 percent with the twelfth half-hour; out-of-sample 1.2 and 1.8 percent), a sign-timing strategy earns 6.67 percent a year at 6.19 percent volatility, Sharpe 1.08, before costs, 1993-2013.
sources.independent_replication: Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021) find the same last-30-minute pattern in 60+ futures 1974-2020.
sources.limitations: Gross of costs, sample ends 2013; effect said stronger on volatile and high-volume days.
sources.market_and_period: SPY and ten other ETFs, 1993-2013, 30-minute returns, gross of costs
sources.project_applicability: Group B predictors (first half-hour with and without overnight, plus the twelfth half-hour) and trading window 15:30-16:00.
sources.reflection: Local sample 2016-2026 is out of sample for the published window; replication target is sign and size of R2, not the 1993-2013 numbers.

sources.applicability: Group C rule, universe filters and stop sizes.
sources.claim: Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz (SSRN 4729284): 5-minute opening range breakout traded only on the top 20 stocks by relative volume, stop at 10 percent of ATR14, flat at close, 2016-2023 about 7,000 US stocks: IRR 41.6 percent, Sharpe 2.81 versus 3.2 percent and 0.48 without the relative-volume filter; 0.08R per trade, commission only.
sources.core_claim: Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz (SSRN 4729284): 5-minute opening range breakout traded only on the top 20 stocks by relative volume, stop at 10 percent of ATR14, flat at close, 2016-2023 about 7,000 US stocks: IRR 41.6 percent, Sharpe 2.81 versus 3.2 percent and 0.48 without the relative-volume filter; 0.08R per trade, commission only.
sources.independent_replication: QuantConnect research (2016 only, 1,000 liquid stocks) reports Sharpe 2.40; its comments flag stop fills one bar late and a win rate near 17 percent.
sources.limitations: No spread or slippage; stop fills in the original are intrabar at the stop price; author-reported.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks 2016-2023, 5-minute bars, commission $0.0035 per share, no spread or slippage
sources.project_applicability: Group C rule, universe filters and stop sizes.
sources.reflection: The cost gap is the whole question here: 9-40 bp per round trip at the open versus 8 bp gross per trade.

sources.applicability: Mechanism and independent replication for groups A and B; says why leveraged ETFs are in the symbol axis.
sources.claim: Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens (JFE 2021): in 60+ futures 1974-2020 the return of the last 30 minutes is positively predicted by the return in the rest of the day; linked to gamma hedging of options market makers and leveraged ETFs; out-of-sample R2 up to about 2.9 percent for equity index futures.
sources.core_claim: Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens (JFE 2021): in 60+ futures 1974-2020 the return of the last 30 minutes is positively predicted by the return in the rest of the day; linked to gamma hedging of options market makers and leveraged ETFs; out-of-sample R2 up to about 2.9 percent for equity index futures.
sources.limitations: Futures not ETFs; effect reverts over following days.
sources.project_applicability: Mechanism and independent replication for groups A and B; says why leveraged ETFs are in the symbol axis.
sources.reflection: Supports a persistent economic cause rather than a one-sample pattern.

sources.claim: QuantConnect research: 2016-only backtest of the stocks-in-play opening range breakout on the 1,000 most liquid US equities gives Sharpe 2.396; comments say stop orders fill on the next minute bar in backtests versus near-instantly live, and win rate is about 17 percent.
sources.core_claim: QuantConnect research: 2016-only backtest of the stocks-in-play opening range breakout on the 1,000 most liquid US equities gives Sharpe 2.396; comments say stop orders fill on the next minute bar in backtests versus near-instantly live, and win rate is about 17 percent.

sources.project_applicability: Third-party fidelity check and the stop-fill semantics variants of group C.
sources.reflection: Stop-fill assumption flips the sign of local tests; both semantics are registered.
